lorundrostat-hypertension.title: Blood-pressure benefit in Launch-HTN
lorundrostat-hypertension.endpoint: Least-squares mean change in automated office systolic blood pressure
lorundrostat-hypertension.population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension taking 2–5 antihypertensive medications
lorundrostat-hypertension.comparisonLabel: Pooled 50 mg daily groups versus placebo
lorundrostat-hypertension.interpretation: The primary office-BP endpoint favored lorundrostat (p<0.001). Negative values represent reductions from baseline.
limitations: The displayed n values are the pooled active and placebo analysis populations, not the total 1,083 randomized participants.
Both active strategies used 50 mg through week 6; this comparison does not establish a benefit from later escalation to 100 mg.
The adjusted difference need not equal subtraction of the rounded arm estimates. BP reduction does not itself demonstrate fewer cardiovascular events.
lorundrostat-hypertension.sourceNote: JAMA, published online June 30, 2025: primary results and Table 2. Original publication inspected during review of the recorded lorundrostat investigation.

lorundrostat-hypertension.title: The safety question: potassium excursions
lorundrostat-hypertension.endpoint: Participants with serum potassium above 6.0 mmol/L
lorundrostat-hypertension.population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension after a standardized background-treatment run-in
lorundrostat-hypertension.comparisonLabel: Fixed dose, dose-adjustment strategy and placebo
lorundrostat-hypertension.interpretation: The paper reports potassium excursions in 5, 7 and 0 participants, respectively. These observed events support a safety-management question despite BP efficacy.
limitations: Percentages are rounded as published; the events are laboratory thresholds, not necessarily serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations.
Escalation to 100 mg was conditional after week 4; the second arm is a dosing strategy, not 100 mg throughout.
Rates from another study cannot be directly compared without accounting for background therapy, eligibility and monitoring.
lorundrostat-hypertension.sourceNote: NEJM abstract, published online April 23, 2025: randomized group sizes and potassium results. The complete article and supplement were not reviewed.

satralizumab-ted.title: SatraGO-1 missed its primary endpoint
satralizumab-ted.endpoint: Proptosis response: ≥2 mm improvement in the study eye, without ≥2 mm worsening in the fellow eye
satralizumab-ted.population: Active thyroid eye disease · Part I full-analysis population
satralizumab-ted.interpretation: The numerical response difference did not meet the prespecified significance threshold (p=0.0715). The confidence interval includes zero.
limitations: The primary analysis used multiple imputation; do not infer integer responder counts from the displayed percentages and n.
The Mantel–Haenszel difference is stratified and need not equal simple subtraction of rounded percentages.
The failed primary endpoint stopped confirmatory hierarchical testing; this trial’s secondary p-values are descriptive. This is the active-TED analysis, not all 131 randomized participants.
satralizumab-ted.sourceNote: ClinicalTrials.gov primary outcome and September 7, 2026 Ophthalmology journal pre-proof. Registry n values are the reported primary-outcome denominators.

satralizumab-ted.title: SatraGO-2 met the same primary endpoint
satralizumab-ted.endpoint: Proptosis response: ≥2 mm improvement in the study eye, without ≥2 mm worsening in the fellow eye
satralizumab-ted.population: Active thyroid eye disease · Part I full-analysis population
satralizumab-ted.interpretation: This trial met its primary endpoint (p=0.0011). The result provides support, while SatraGO-1’s primary failure remains relevant to the total evidence.
limitations: The primary analysis used multiple imputation; displayed percentages are not raw responder counts.
The stratified difference differs from subtraction of the displayed percentages. The 95.03% confidence level is intentional.
These are separate randomized trials; comparing their placebo bars does not prove the cause of discordant findings. The n values exclude inactive-TED participants.
satralizumab-ted.sourceNote: ClinicalTrials.gov primary outcome and September 7, 2026 Ophthalmology journal pre-proof. The two trials are displayed separately, without pooling.

zanzalintinib-mcrc.title: Overall-population survival result
zanzalintinib-mcrc.population: Intention-to-treat population with previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer; MSI-H/dMMR disease excluded
zanzalintinib-mcrc.timepoint: April 30, 2025 data cutoff · median follow-up 18 months
zanzalintinib-mcrc.interpretation: The later results publication reports a significant ITT survival endpoint (p=0.0045). The HR describes the survival comparison over follow-up, not the ratio of median months.
limitations: Median values summarize survival distributions; these bars are not Kaplan–Meier curves or a predicted survival trajectory.
An earlier design publication used a different testing hierarchy. The final operative amended SAP was not retrieved; the old design alone cannot invalidate the later ITT result.
This is combination evidence, with no zanzalintinib-alone arm, and does not generalize to MSI-H/dMMR disease.
zanzalintinib-mcrc.sourceNote: The Lancet results abstract indexed in PubMed (PMID 41130252), published online October 20, 2025; earlier design publication and current registry supply the testing-plan caveat.

zanzalintinib-mcrc.title: Final non-liver-metastasis endpoint remained nonsignificant
zanzalintinib-mcrc.population: Trial participants without active liver metastases at baseline; non-MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer
zanzalintinib-mcrc.interpretation: Despite the numerical median difference, the final NLM endpoint was nonsignificant (p=0.1185). This is not evidence of no effect or of harm.
limitations: These are the final NLM estimates, not the earlier interim HR 0.79. The final-analysis release does not provide arm denominators, so none are displayed.
NLM means no active liver metastases at baseline, not no history of liver metastases. This subset must not be substituted for the ITT population.
Median differences and hazard ratios describe different aspects of survival. The operative statistical-testing plan remains an unresolved diligence question.
zanzalintinib-mcrc.sourceNote: Exelixis June 22, 2026 final NLM results release. Sponsor-reported final analysis; reviewed alongside the earlier design publication.

bezuclastinib-gist.title: Progression-free survival in PEAK
bezuclastinib-gist.endpoint: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review
bezuclastinib-gist.population: Patients with GIST previously treated with imatinib
bezuclastinib-gist.interpretation: Cogent reported a significant PFS benefit (p<0.0001). This supports the combination in imatinib-treated GIST, rather than bezuclastinib monotherapy.
limitations: Overall survival was immature in this disclosure; PFS is not an established overall-survival benefit.
Arm denominators and the exact analysis cutoff were not established from this release and are omitted. Registry enrollment is not used as an efficacy denominator.
These are reported medians, not a reconstructed survival curve. The HR is not the ratio of those medians.
bezuclastinib-gist.sourceNote: Cogent’s May 28, 2026 sponsor release, Clinical Data section. Values are sponsor-reported and are not an FDA conclusion.

giredestrant-early-breast.title: Three-year invasive disease-free survival
giredestrant-early-breast.endpoint: Estimated invasive disease-free survival; excludes second primary non-breast cancers
giredestrant-early-breast.population: Medium- or high-risk stage I–III ER-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer
giredestrant-early-breast.comparisonLabel: Adjuvant giredestrant versus standard endocrine therapy
giredestrant-early-breast.interpretation: The reported three-year estimates differ by 2.8 percentage points. The 30% relative hazard reduction (p=0.0014) is a different quantity, not a 30-point absolute benefit.
limitations: These are survival estimates at three years, not simple proportions of all enrolled patients or a complete survival curve.
The HR summarizes follow-up rather than only the three-year timepoint. Overall-survival data were immature.
The comparator is standard endocrine therapy, not placebo. Arm-level risk-set counts and intervals around the three-year estimates are not supplied here.
giredestrant-early-breast.sourceNote: Roche’s June 2, 2026 sponsor release: primary iDFS results and study definition. The absolute difference is simple subtraction of the two reported point estimates.

atezolizumab-colon-adjuvant.title: Disease-free survival in molecularly selected colon cancer
atezolizumab-colon-adjuvant.population: Resected stage III colon cancer with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR)
atezolizumab-colon-adjuvant.comparisonLabel: Atezolizumab + FOLFOX6 regimen versus FOLFOX6 alone
atezolizumab-colon-adjuvant.interpretation: Roche reported a 10-percentage-point difference between rounded three-year DFS estimates. This is a disease-free-survival result in dMMR stage III colon cancer.
limitations: The sponsor release rounds estimates to whole percentages; no extra decimals or confidence intervals are inferred.
The experimental regimen includes six months of combination treatment followed by six months of atezolizumab alone; the control receives six months of FOLFOX6.
DFS does not establish an overall-survival benefit. Results do not generalize to all colorectal cancers. Total enrollment 712 is not an arm-specific risk-set denominator.
atezolizumab-colon-adjuvant.sourceNote: Roche’s June 11, 2026 sponsor release, ATOMIC results and trial description. The plotted values preserve the disclosure’s rounding.
